summary.headline: Navin Fluorine Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 44% YoY to INR1,044-1,045 crore, with EBITDA up 73% and PAT up 108% to INR243 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 44% YoY to about INR1,045 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR357 crore (34.2% margin, up 566 bps YoY) and PAT of INR243 crore. All three verticals (HPP, specialty chemicals, CDMO) grew strongly, and the company became net debt free during the quarter. Management announced a new INR90 crore advanced materials adoption capex and a Phase 2 CDMO cGMP capex of INR125 crore. Management guided to a 32-33% EBITDA margin range going forward (plus/minus 1%), while flagging gross margin pressure from higher raw material costs.

segments.name: HPP (HFCs/fluorochemicals)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR540 crore, up 33% YoY on healthy volume growth and improved realisations; management describes HFC pricing as constructive given demand-supply dynamics.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (agchem)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR325 crore, up 48% YoY. Management plans campaign orders for 4-5 agchem molecules this year; LatAm agchem pricing pressure persists, and EBITDA is not expected to return to the old ~30% level.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR180 crore, up 82% YoY. Pipeline of 30-40 molecules, about 10 late stage; 3-4 molecules expected to get FDA readouts in the next 8-12 months. Management targets about $100 million for FY27.

segments.name: Advanced materials (incubating within HPP)
segments.commentary: Not separately reported. Chemours liquid cooling project targeted for completion by end Q2 FY27; Chemours reportedly sold about $1 million of two-phase cooling liquid in the quarter (per analyst). DRDO TDF partnership announced.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in the 32-33% range (plus/minus 1%) on a normalised basis over the next one to two years, supported by HFC, debottlenecking and Chemours capacity.
CDMO FY27 target of about $100 million reiterated; FY29 asset turn of 3x on INR288 crore cGMP4 capex stated as the near-term view.
Gross margin dipped about 100 bps QoQ from Q4 FY26 on raw material costs; management said price pass-through will lag.
Advanced materials adoption capex (INR90 crore) to be done in two phases, first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 for commercial-scale qualification; not included in any return projections.
Growth visibility beyond FY28 depends on the current capex cycle (cGMP Phase 1, adoption capacity, Chemours).
capex_capacity: New advanced materials adoption capex of INR90 crore, internally funded, to be set up at Surat; creates two core platforms and augments analytical equipment.
CDMO cGMP4 Phase 2 capex of INR125 crore (part of INR288 crore approved Feb 2024), operationalisation expected Q4 FY27; Phase 1 operational in Q3 FY26. Dedicated to European CDMO partner.

HFC capacity addition of up to 15,000 MT of R32 on track for Q3 FY27; company currently has about 9,000-10,000 MT and total would be about 25,000 MT. Revenue band of INR600-825 crore cited from original capex approval.
MPP debottlenecking at Dahej on track for completion by Q3 FY27; management cited 2x asset turn.
AHF capacity of 60,000 MT between Surat and Dahej seen as adequate for the next 4-5 years; AHF commissioned in the subsidiary NFASL.
Renewable project of INR15.73 crore (14.9 MW hybrid) expected to supply more than 60% of energy needs once operational.
demand_pricing: R32: management expects a 35-45% contracted share of capacity over five years; a couple of contracts signed and more at a late stage.
R32 long-term demand said to double over a decade while quota-driven supply shrinks by half; Indian oversupply expected for about five years with exports to global market.
Specialty chemicals: volume recovering, but pricing pressure persists in LatAm; 13-14 new molecules launched last year and 5 new molecules being participated in, of which 3 are patented.
HFO supply to Honeywell: asset commercialised July 2022; original seven-year term with a three-year extension at Honeywell's option, so runway beyond FY29.
Management stated that raw material cost inflation is rising amid global war tensions and supply chain risk.

qa_highlights.question: Advanced materials: end-use applications, and growth beyond FY28 given current capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is to make advanced materials a material business unit by end of decade, modelled on today's CDMO. Focus on data centers, electronics, semiconductors, defence; the adoption capex is phased, with first phase complete around mid-Q4 FY27 to start commercial-scale qualification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR90 crore adoption capex a pilot or commercial scale, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said five products are already lab-approved and this capex takes them to commercial-scale qualification; not a pilot. No asset turn is assumed in numbers for the INR90 crore.

qa_highlights.question: R32 pricing and India capacity additions versus quota start in Jan 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give pricing; said it will stay the lowest-cost R32 producer through its integrated HF chain and renewable power. Expects India oversupply for about five years and exports.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary (NFASL) margin fall about 12 pp QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Campaign mix differs quarter to quarter, and AHF transfers from Dahej to Surat are at arm's-length, so value shows up at Navin Fluorine (NFIL) level; group margin remains solid.

qa_highlights.question: CDMO: is the new capacity dedicated, and is the MSA for an extra molecule with the same customer?
qa_highlights.answer: New capacity dedicated to European CDMO partner; an MSA for an extra molecule in the same supply chain takes Navin to API minus 1. Also working on an early-phase molecule with the same customer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $100 million CDMO target for FY27 still on track, and is INR900 crore cGMP capex math right?
qa_highlights.answer: $100 million target reiterated as on track. Management confirmed the 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29, and that Phase 1 and Phase 2 combined are about INR900 crore is not exactly right; the INR288 crore figure is the approved base (3x = about INR900 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: HFC contracts, AHF utilisation, and the reason for the margin mix change YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: A couple of R32 contracts signed, with more near conclusion; balanced approach kept. Margin mix explained by HF price highs in Q1 FY26 and rising RM costs now; gross margin down about 100 bps QoQ, offset by fixed-cost productivity.

risks_watch: R32 pricing and contracted share: management targets 35-45% of capacity under five-year contracts, with a couple signed and more near conclusion; watch for contract signings and any price disclosure, since pricing was not given.

Gross margin pressure: gross margin fell about 100 bps QoQ on raw material inflation, with price pass-through expected to lag; watch whether the 32-33% EBITDA range (plus/minus 1%) holds as the HFC, debottlenecking and Chemours capacity come on line.

Advanced materials execution: INR90 crore adoption capex is phased, with first phase around mid-Q4 FY27 and commercialisation of about five lab-approved products; no asset turn assumed, so timing and qualification outcomes are key.

CDMO readouts: 3-4 molecules expected to get FDA readouts in the next 8-12 months after one readout did not go well; $100 million FY27 target and 3x asset turn on INR288 crore by FY29 depend on these.
Subsidiary NFASL margin swing: standalone-to-consolidated EBITDA margin gap was about 12 pp QoQ, attributed to campaign mix and arm's-length AHF transfers; watch for downstream capacity at NFASL.
Specialty chemicals (agchem) LatAm pricing pressure persists; management said EBITDA will not return to the old ~30% level, and campaign orders for 4-5 molecules are expected this year.
key_quotes: The revenue of the quarter grew 44% Y -o-Y to INR1,044 crores and EBITDA stood at INR357 crores, up 73% year-on-year and PAT at INR243 crores, registering a growth of 108% year-on-year.
I don't think this is a case of being equal.
Yes, the $100 million is very much on track.
So as we get into more HF you would see that overall, the margin will remain at a group level quite solid.
So, for Navin, the operating leverage on 32 is going to be fantastic.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, capex pipeline and the 32-33% margin range, but cautious and evasive on R32 pricing, the DRDO order economics, AHF split and CDMO molecule-level details, which management repeatedly declined to quantify. Management leaned on "wait and see" framing for Chemours scale-up and on the 15-month window.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue up 44% and EBITDA up 73%; FY27 CDMO target of about $100m is reiterated and R32 capacity of up to 15,000 MT is on track for Q3 FY27, but the brief gives no company-wide revenue growth number and the 32-33% EBITDA margin guide is a margin, not growth, target.
